label: <DEL> step of length-9 sequences
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t=9) of length-9 sequences: every dev activation is there, and it never fires in the original or copy phases or at the <DEL> of shorter sequences. Within that context it fires on only about 20% of sequences, and which ones depends weakly on content spread over many tokens. The first token (the one about to be output) matters most: n, h, f, e, x, u, r, d give 2-5x lift, and n starts most of the top examples. The last original token adds a little (l, 1, q, a). Adding token lists raised dev F1 only from 0.33 to about 0.47, so content gating was left out of the predicate. Magnitude is not explained beyond the first-token skew.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: l, 1, q, a, f, p; least: e, o, w, t) and the token being output (most: n, h, f, u, x, r; least: p, a, -, 3); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=9, to_go=8, t=9.
